title: Lesson 1 - Gradient Descent and the Loss Surface
author: Sample course (bundled with the project)

segments.text: welcome to the first lesson of this short course on training neural networks. today we only care about one question,
which is how a network gets to the right numbers for its weights. the answer is gradient descent. start with
the loss function. the loss is a single number telling you how wrong the network is right now. for regression
we use mean squared error, which averages the squared differences between prediction and truth. for classification we use cross entropy,
which punishes a confident wrong answer far more harshly than a hesitant one. now picture every weight as a coordinate
and the loss as the height of a landscape above those coordinates. training is walking downhill on that landscape until
you reach a valley. the direction downhill comes from the gradient, which is the vector of partial derivatives of the
loss with respect to each weight. the gradient points uphill, so we step in the negative gradient direction. the size
of that step is the learning rate. we will come back to the learning rate properly in lesson three, because
choosing it badly is the single most common reason training fails. for now just remember that it controls how far
you move on each step. next lesson we will look at how the gradient is actually computed for a network
